facts.text: The package registers FloatingMiaGraspInsole-v0 with entry point deformable_gym.envs.floating_mia_grasp_env:FloatingMiaGraspEnv, object_name 'insole_on_conveyor_belt/back' and observable_object_pos True
The documented example creates the environment with gymnasium.make('FloatingMiaGraspInsole-v0')
The floating Mia action space bounds the 3 end-effector position offsets by +-0.0005 and the 4 orientation offsets by +-0.000005
The action space has 10 values: 3 position offsets, 4 orientation offsets and 3 finger commands
The finger bounds of the action space are selected from the motor array with actuated_finger_ids [0, 1, 5]
The observation is the end-effector pose (7 values), 3 finger joint positions and 6 force readings; with observable_object_pos it appends 3 object position values
The observation space bounds the position by -2..2 (z 0..2), the quaternion by -1..1, the three finger positions by the motor limits, the six forces by -10..10 and the object position by -2..2
The default horizon is 100 environment steps
BaseBulletEnv.step terminates the episode when step_counter reaches the horizon
The simulation registers a time_step subsystem at 100 Hz, with a default time_delta of 0.001 s
BaseBulletEnv.reset accepts an options mapping with a hard_reset key that reloads the simulation
BaseBulletEnv.reset passes seed and options to gymnasium's Env.reset through super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
The reward is 0.0 until the episode terminates; on termination it is +1.0 when the released object's height is at least 0.9 and -1.0 otherwise
The initial hand pose is position (0.03, -0.025, 1.0) with Euler angles (-pi/8, pi, 0) converted by pybullet.getQuaternionFromEuler
MiaHand._correct_index_limit sets the index finger's lower limit to 0.0 and keeps its upper limit
The j_index_fle URDF limit is -1.399999976 to 1.399999976
The j_little_fle URDF limit is 0 to 1.396260023
The j_thumb_opp URDF limit is -0.628 to 0.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 are passed to the environment reset; the upstream environment has a fixed initial hand pose, so this fake's state is deterministic, but its trajectories are not the upstream PyBullet trajectories and no seed makes them so

gaps: scripted stand-in for a PyBullet soft-body grasping task: no contacts, deformation, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; finger positions are copied from the command, forces stay zero and the object does not move
the fake's terminal reward is a placeholder; the upstream reward releases the object, advances the deformable simulation and tests the object mesh height (deformable_gym/envs/grasp_env.py:60-79)

the published action bounds select motor-array entries 0, 1 and 5 while the commands are applied to the actuated real joints (index, mrl, thumb); the fake keeps the published bounds and does not model the joint mapping
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (the 100 Hz time_step subsystem of deformable_gym/envs/base_env.py:72) only
the fake returns 19-value Python lists; upstream returns numpy float64 observation arrays and has a render_mode with a PyBullet GUI
the fake was never compared with a run of the upstream environment; pybullet, numpy and pytransform3d are not needed by the gate and were not installed
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
